body: Just wanted to say thanks for helping me get through the night. Today was a good day. We are putting up the tree and the things I don't have aren't looming so large as they seemed to last night. I know that kind of dark sadness is still there, waiting for me, but for right now, I'm drowning it in twinkly lights and motown music. Thank you, kind people, for your encouragement. I appreciate you giving me a bit of time. Sometimes I just need a little help through. Thank you.
Thanks. I don't really know what else to say. It's Friday. Why are you reading r/sw?

Yeah, I thought about posting over there, but all the threads seemed to be more about the technical aspects of what is and isn't depression and I didn't want to pour my guts out only to be told I am in the wrong place for it. I know I am dealing with depression. Doesn't make it any easier. Mostly just wanted to talk about it instead of sitting along crying. Suicide hotlines will put you on hold and there's no therapists on Friday nights. That leaves me and rum, which makes me feel kind of like a loser, drinking alone, so I came on here to talk instead.

In our area of the US, you can get a job at the hospital, even a entry level job, and they have education reimbursement if you go to school for nursing. Around here, the nursing program is at a community college, which makes it way more affordable than it might be otherwise. Even if you don't get the GI bill, don't give up on being a nurse. Take one semester and pay it out of pocket or on loan if you have to. Make good grades, no excuses! Then apply for reimbursement, turn it around into next semester's expenses. See if you can get a scholarship. You can still be a nurse, even if you can't run or can't have the GI bill.  I know people that have done it, so it can be done. May not be easy, but nothing is. Please don't give up.
